title: Coordinate cup products compute trivial discrete-lattice derived invariants
statement:
Let $R$ be any commutative condensed ring on the small coherent profinite site [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, def-weil-size-convention], and use ordinary internal module derived categories [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $r\geq0$ and let $D=\mathbf Z^r$ with the discrete topology, acting trivially on $R$ [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. For $1\le i\le r$ let $d_i:\underline D\to(R,+)$ be the additive condensed map induced sectionwise by $(n_1,\ldots,n_r)\mapsto n_i1_R$. Write $\delta_i:R[-1]\to R\Gamma_{R,D}(R[0])$ for its connecting character class, using the cup product and the connecting-class normalization of [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus].

Let $\mathcal E_{R,r}=\bigoplus_{I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}}R[-|I|]$, represented by the zero-differential complex whose degree $q$ term is the finite sum indexed by $q$-element subsets. The morphism
$$\chi_{R,r}:\mathcal E_{R,r}\longrightarrow R\Gamma_{R,D}(R[0])$$
which is the unit on $I=\varnothing$ and $\delta_{i_1}\smile\cdots\smile\delta_{i_q}$ on the summand for $I=\{i_1<\cdots<i_q\}$ is an isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Mod}_R)$. This specifies the actual derived morphism, including its cup-product normalization. For $r=0$ it is the identity $R[0]$. The zero ring is allowed; no characteristic, completeness, or flatness assumption on $R$ is imposed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-discrete-lattice-koszul-resolution] to the trivial action on $P=R$. Every $T_i-1$ is zero, so its displayed differential vanishes and $K_R(R;1)=\mathcal E_{R,r}$ with exactly the subset indexing of the statement. Choose the comparison supplied by [lem-sfb-lattice-koszul-triangulated-cup-comparison]; denote its component on $R$ by $\lambda_R$. It is an isomorphism and its restriction to the degree-zero summand is the invariant inclusion followed by the derived unit. Let $u_I:R[-|I|]\to K_R(R;1)$ be the chain inclusion with coefficient $1$ on subset $I$ and zero on all other subsets of that size.

proof.text: For each coordinate $i$, take the character extension $0\to R\xrightarrow{x\mapsto(x,0)}E_i\xrightarrow{(x,y)\mapsto y}R\to0$ from [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus], where $E_i=R\oplus R$ and the $j$th standard generator acts by $T_j(x,y)=(x+\mathbf1_{j=i}y,y)$. These operators commute, since composing them adds their upper-right entries; they are invertible by negating that entry. The sequence is exact on underlying internal modules and therefore equivariantly exact by the same cited node. Applying the Koszul construction gives a degreewise split short exact sequence of complexes; in every subset component choose $s(y)=(0,y)$ and $\pi(x,y)=x$. This splitting is needed only as a splitting of underlying modules, not of actions.

source.place: Paragraph (3), ordinary open direct image; algebraic discrete-lattice normalization in the tame-boundary calculation, below the unit route. Agent expansion, not an assertion proved in the blueprint paragraph. Step 2.

proof.text: By [lem-sc-p1-split-ses-boundary-comparison], the actual derived connecting morphism for the sequence of step 2 is the localization of the split cochain boundary with component $\pi^{n+1}d_{K(E_i)}^n s^n$. In degree zero its composite with $u_\varnothing$ has component at $\{j\}$ equal to $\pi(T_j-1)(0,1)=\mathbf1_{j=i}1_R$. Thus, after shifting, this composite is precisely $u_{\{i\}}:R[-1]\to K_R(R;1)$. This is equality of derived morphisms represented by chain maps, not only equality of degree-one cohomology classes. The connecting-morphism compatibility of [lem-sfb-lattice-koszul-triangulated-cup-comparison], together with the defining normalization of the character in [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus], consequently gives $\delta_i=\lambda_R\circ u_{\{i\}}$.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-lattice-koszul-triangulated-cup-comparison] with the coefficient algebra $B=R$ and trivial action. Its flatness condition holds since $R\otimes_R-$ is the identity functor. In its displayed pairing every $T_A$ is the identity. If $I=\{i_1<\cdots<i_q\}$, multiplication of $u_{\{i_1\}},\ldots,u_{\{i_q\}}$ in this order gives $u_I$: inductively, when appending $i_k$, the only nonzero decomposition has $A=\{i_1,\ldots,i_{k-1}\}$ and $C=\{i_k\}$, and there are no pairs $c<a$, so its sign is $+1$ and its coefficient is $1$. All other subset components are zero. This proves the claim by induction, starting with the empty-subset unit. The derived pairing equality in the cited node and step 3 now give $\delta_{i_1}\smile\cdots\smile\delta_{i_q}=\lambda_R\circ u_I$, using the canonical identifications of tensor products of the single-term shifts.

proof.text: Step 4 identifies the specified morphism $\chi_{R,r}$ with $\lambda_R$ on every summand of the finite direct sum $\mathcal E_{R,r}$, including the unit summand. The universal property of that direct sum gives $\chi_{R,r}=\lambda_R$, so it is an isomorphism. For $r=0$ there is only the empty subset and the chosen comparison is the identity. For the zero ring every term and every displayed morphism is the zero object and its unique identity; all computations remain valid. No integer has been divided out and no assumption on the characteristic or topology of $R$ entered the proof.
